cover.caption: Kona ville selge kua selv, og hjem kom hun full av fjær.
cover.alt: Kona går hjemover på den støvete veien, full av fjær, og ser forundret på armene sine. Langt borte ligger den lille gården.

characters.name: Kona
characters.description: Sta og lettlurt, havner i trøbbel når hun skal selge kua, og blir så forvirret at hun ikke kjenner seg selv igjen.
characters.look: A cheerful, dreamy farm wife of about forty-five, a little round, with a long ski-jump nose, big round blue eyes that always look amazed, rosy cheeks, a pleased little smile and two long, thin straw-yellow plaits tied at the ends with red wool. She wears a rust-orange wool skirt, a black bodice laced with red ribbon over a white blouse with wide sleeves, a big white apron with one deep front pocket and wooden-soled shoes.

characters.name: Kona med tjære og fjær
characters.description: Kona etter slakterens puss: full av tjære og fjær fra topp til tå, så hun tror hun må være en stor, underlig fugl.
characters.look: The Wife after the Butcher's prank: the same cheerful woman of about forty-five with a long ski-jump nose, big round amazed blue eyes and two long straw-yellow plaits tied with red wool, in her rust-orange skirt, black laced bodice and white apron, but now sticky with black tar and covered from head to toe with fluffy white, grey and brown feathers on her clothes, arms, hair and cheeks, so that she looks like a big, ruffled bird.

characters.name: Mannen fra Ringerike
characters.description: En fattig, men kvikk bonde som bruker vett og frekke løgner for å skaffe penger og komme seg ut av knipa.
characters.look: A lean, wiry farmer of about forty-five with a narrow, clever face, a long straight nose, lively dark eyes with laugh crinkles, a patient half-smile, a short, neat black beard and cropped black hair. He wears a small black cap with a turned-up brim, a faded cornflower-blue coat with big pockets and brass buttons, and patched grey trousers tucked into worn brown boots.

characters.name: Slakteren
characters.description: En slu bymann som utnytter konas dumskap, byr på mat og brennevin og lurer henne skikkelig.
characters.look: A huge, barrel-chested butcher of about fifty with a round, shiny red face, a bulbous nose, twinkling little black eyes, bushy black eyebrows, a sly grin and a big, round, bushy black beard. He wears a small white linen cap, a red shirt with the sleeves rolled up over thick arms and a long white apron with blue stripes, and he always has a string of sausages slung over one shoulder.

characters.name: Kjerringa som vil bære inn sol
characters.description: Ei kjerring i ei ny tømmerstue uten vinduer, som springer ut og inn med ei sil for å bære inn sola.
characters.look: A tiny, quick, bird-like woman of about thirty with a small round face, a pointed chin, bright eager green eyes, rosy cheeks and a mass of glossy black curls tied up in a sunflower-yellow kerchief. She wears an apricot-orange dress with a white apron and red shoes, and she always carries a big, round, shallow sieve with a wooden rim and a bottom full of tiny holes.

characters.name: Kjerringa på gården
characters.description: Ei godtroende kjerring som har vært gift tre ganger, hver gang med en Per. Hun hører «Himmerike» når mannen sier Ringerike, og sender klær, sølvpenger og hest til Per den andre i himmelen.
characters.look: A tall, big, well-fed farm wife of about sixty with a large round face, a double chin, pink cheeks, a big mouth always open to talk, bright little inquisitive eyes and iron-grey ringlets under a large round black bonnet trimmed with lace and tied under her chins. She wears a wine-red wool dress with silver buttons and a green silk shawl, and she always holds a long brass ear trumpet to one ear.

characters.name: Per den tredje
characters.description: Kjerringas tredje mann, en gretten bonde som setter etter mannen fra Ringerike, men blir lurt til å ligge og stirre opp i skyene.
characters.look: A tall, heavy, grumpy farmer of about fifty with a long, sour face, a drooping lower lip, a big red nose, deep frown lines, bristly black eyebrows and a short, stiff iron-grey beard like a doormat. He wears a floppy black stocking cap, a patched leather jerkin over a rust-red shirt, brown knee breeches and tall muddy boots.

illustrations.fullPrompt:
Reference images:
- Image 1: model sheet for the Farmer, the same character seen from three sides. Keep the Farmer's face, hair, body shape, age, colours and clothes exactly as shown. Draw the Farmer only once, in the pose this picture needs, and ignore the sheet's layout and plain background.
- Image 2: model sheet for the Wife, the same character seen from three sides. Keep the Wife's face, hair, body shape, age, colours and clothes exactly as shown. Draw the Wife only once, in the pose this picture needs, and ignore the sheet's layout and plain background.
- Image 3: setting reference for the Little Farm. Keep its landforms, buildings, colours and key details, and choose the viewpoint and framing this picture needs.

Create one new illustration for an illustrated folk-tale book, showing the moment described below.

Picture: At the Little Farm under a heavy grey sky, the Farmer has just pulled up in the loaded cart behind the blue-grey dappled horse, with the chestnut-brown horse tied on behind. He stares at the brown field: it has been ploughed, and white salt glitters in every furrow. The Wife stands proudly at the end of the furrows with an empty wooden bucket on her hip and empty sacks at her feet.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Farmer: A lean, wiry farmer of about forty-five with a narrow, clever face, a long straight nose, lively dark eyes with laugh crinkles, a patient half-smile, a short, neat black beard and cropped black hair. He wears a small black cap with a turned-up brim, a faded cornflower-blue coat with big pockets and brass buttons, and patched grey trousers tucked into worn brown boots.
- the Wife: A cheerful, dreamy farm wife of about forty-five, a little round, with a long ski-jump nose, big round blue eyes that always look amazed, rosy cheeks, a pleased little smile and two long, thin straw-yellow plaits tied at the ends with red wool. She wears a rust-orange wool skirt, a black bodice laced with red ribbon over a white blouse with wide sleeves, a big white apron with one deep front pocket and wooden-soled shoes.

Setting:
- the Little Farm: A small, poor farm on a gentle slope: a low grey log cottage with a turf roof, a tiny cowshed, and a little storehouse standing on four stone legs with a steep roof of wooden shingles. In front lies one small brown field ringed by a split-rail fence, with a few birches in their first spring leaf and yellow coltsfoot along the fence.

Story world: Old rural Norway at sowing time, in the Ringerike country. The Farmer and his Wife have a small, poor farm with one brown field. A dusty road leads to the market town, where the Butcher has his shop and yard. Far along the roads stand a brand-new log house with no windows that still smells of resin, a small plain cottage, and a big farm with a storehouse and a field being ploughed. The Wife's hen is a scrawny, half-bald speckled hen. The widow's blue horse is a sturdy blue-grey dappled horse with a black mane and tail, harnessed to a small two-wheeled wooden cart; Per the Third's horse is chestnut-brown. The sieve is a big, round, shallow sieve with a wooden rim.

This story's season, light and colours: Late April at sowing time: a dry, breezy spring with pale sunshine and drifting cloud, bare brown fields and fresh dark furrows, birches in their first mouse-ear green, the last grey snow patches in the shade of the spruce, yellow coltsfoot in the ditches and dusty roads. At the end, a heavy grey sky that promises rain. Accents: the Wife's rust-orange skirt, white feathers and the blue-grey horse.

Art style: Classic Norwegian folk-tale book illustration: fine pen-and-ink line work with transparent watercolour washes on warm, slightly textured off-white paper, in the tradition of 19th-century Scandinavian book illustration, like the plates of an old printed book of folk tales, with a deep red that comes back as the accent. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Naturalistic proportions and expressive, characterful faces; every character has their own face, build, age and hair exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Muted natural palette of fjord teal, slate blue, moss green, lichen grey, honey ochre, lingonberry red, ink black and birch white, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, with the warm cream paper showing through the washes, with dramatic Nordic light: low sun, long shadows, blue dusk and firelight. Old rural Norway: dark spruce and pine forests, steep mountains, fjords, turf-roofed log farms, carved wood, homespun wool and linen. Trolls are enormous, ancient and earthy, like pieces of the landscape come alive, made of moss, bark, stone and lichen, and more grotesque-comic than frightening. Kings and princesses wear modest medieval finery. Careful composition with depth and atmosphere, one clear focal point and room for the landscape. Not cute or cartoonish, not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.
- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.
- Suitable for readers of all ages: no blood, wounds or gore, and no killing shown. Show danger and cruelty through atmosphere, posture and suspense, never through injury.
- Draw each named character only once.
- Show exactly the number of people, animals and things the description asks for, and no extra people.
- One clear moment that reads at a glance, as a single full-bleed picture with no border, frame or comic panels.
